prompts.task_spec:
Online bin packing. Items arrive one at a time and each must be placed immediately, without knowledge of future items, into a bin of fixed integer capacity; the goal is to use as few bins as possible. You will write the scoring heuristic that decides where each item goes. For every arriving item the packer calls priority(item, bins), where item is the item size (an integer) and bins is a numpy array with the remaining capacity of every bin in which the item fits, listed in the order in which the bins were created; bins that are still unused appear in this array with their full capacity. The item is placed into the bin with the highest score (the first such bin on ties). Use only numpy (imported as np) and the math module.

```python
import numpy as np


def priority(item: float, bins: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Returns priority with which we want to add item to each bin.

    Args:
        item: Size of item to be added to the bin.
        bins: Array of capacity for each bin.

    Return:
        Array of same size as bins with priority score of each bin.
    """
```

Write the complete function in one Python code block.

instr.INSTR_LONG: Make a fully novel algorithm never seen before. First explain your idea in about 2,000 words, then give the complete function.

BF: putting each item into the bin that it would leave with the least spare room
choosing, among the bins the item fits into, the one whose remaining capacity after placing the item is smallest
placing each item where the leftover space in the chosen bin is minimised
FF: putting each item into the earliest-created bin that has room for it
scanning the bins in the order they were created and placing the item into the first one it fits into
always preferring the oldest bin that can still take the item
WF: putting each item into the already-used bin with the most spare room, and opening a new bin only when no used bin has room
choosing, among the partly filled bins the item fits into, the one with the largest remaining capacity
placing each item into the emptiest partly filled bin that can take it
AWF: putting each item into the already-used bin with the second-most spare room (or into the only used bin that has room), and opening a new bin only when no used bin has room
choosing, among the partly filled bins the item fits into, the one with the second-largest remaining capacity
placing each item into the second-emptiest partly filled bin that can take it
LF: putting each item into the most recently created bin that already holds items and has room for it
scanning the partly filled bins from the newest to the oldest and placing the item into the first one it fits into
always preferring the newest partly filled bin that can still take the item
RF: putting each item into a partly filled bin chosen uniformly at random among those that have room for it, and opening a new bin only when none has room
choosing at random, with equal probability, one of the partly filled bins the item fits into
placing each item into a randomly picked partly filled bin that can take it
